subject: Emotions
title: Microexpressions
description: A micro-lesson that makes Microexpressions usable.

hook.text: A smile flashes across a suspect's face for one-fifth of a second during questioning. The detective catches it.

buildup.text: Paul Ekman discovered microexpressions—involuntary facial movements lasting 1/25th to 1/5th of a second.

discovery.text: They reveal concealed emotions. A microexpression of contempt during 'I love you' betrays the speaker's true feeling.

twist.text: Most people are terrible at reading them without training. Accuracy rates average around 50%—basically coin flips.

climax.text: Training raises accuracy to over 80%. Ekman's FACS system catalogs 43 facial muscles used in emotional expression.

punchline.text: The face can lie. But not for more than a fifth of a second.
